title: dsh-run-plan-v1
description: Epic P4-03's RunPlan: the compiled, data-only plan a run executes. must[0] names its ten fields and this document is their shape; `packages/run/run-plan/src/types.ts` mirrors it. Seven of the ten reference vocabulary the tree already carries — objectives a TaskGoalRef, constraints a TaskConstraint with its hard/soft strength, modelRoutes a ModelSelection, worlds a WorldSpecDigest, budgets the eight BudgetAmounts dimensions, approvalGates an ApprovalRef, verification a VerificationRef — and are written here as references, not restatements. Three had no existing vocabulary and are defined here for the first time: contextTopology, agentGraph and recovery. must[2] is enforced structurally: every property is closed and every leaf is data, so nothing in a plan can carry an expression, a script or a module path to execute. must[4]'s ABI promise is what `schemaVersion` and `verificationContractRef.version` exist for: P7-01 extends the contract by raising its version, never by changing a field's meaning.

schemaVersion.description: The RunPlan ABI this document speaks. A reader that does not know the version refuses the plan rather than reading fields it may misunderstand (must[4]).

planId.description: sha256 of the plan's normalized inputs, lowercase hex, the way `TaskProfileRef` and `WorldSpecDigest` are formed: the same normalized inputs produce the same id, and any change produces a different one (acceptance[2]). Never chosen by a caller.

objectives.description: What the run is for, each traceable to the goal message it came from.

constraints.description: What the run must or should respect. `strength` is the field acceptance[0]'s minimal conflict set is computed over: an unsatisfiable `hard` constraint enters the set, a `soft` one does not.

modelRoutes.description: Which model serves which node, as a `ModelSelection` (`packages/core/agent/src/model-selection.ts`). A node with no route takes the deployment's default, which is resolved at run time and is deliberately not recorded here.

contextTopology.description: Which node may read what another node produced. No existing type carries this, so it is defined here: a set of directed channels, each naming what it carries and how long the receiver may keep it.

agentGraph.description: The nodes the run executes and the order they may execute in. Every node names the TaskProfile requirement it exists to satisfy, which is acceptance[1]'s traceability.

worlds.description: The execution worlds nodes run in, each pinned by its `WorldSpecDigest` rather than by a restated spec, so a world that changed is a different digest.

budgets.description: Ceilings over the eight dimensions `BudgetAmounts` names (`packages/execution/resource-budget/src/types.ts`).

approvalGates.description: Points where the run stops until an Approval entity settles, named by `ApprovalRef` (`packages/run/run/src/types.ts`).

verification.description: What must be verified, named by `VerificationRef`, and under which versioned contract. `verificationContractRef` is must[3]'s extension point: P7-01 supplies a fuller contract by raising `version`, without changing what a plan of an earlier version meant.

recovery.description: What the run does when a node fails. No existing type covers this — `RunResumeDecision` is about resuming a run someone stopped, not about a failure — so it is defined here as a per-node policy plus an explicit terminal disposition.

terminal.description: What the run does when no rule applies: stop and keep the record, or stop and roll the compensations back.

goalRef.description: The goal message a field is traceable to, as `TaskGoalRef` (`packages/run/task-profile/src/types.ts`).

goalRound.description: The entered goal this message continues, present only when the message is a continuation round. Spelled as the three members `TaskGoalRef` carries, because that type spells them out on purpose: taking the goal source's object whole would land a later field in a plan, and therefore in its id, without anyone deciding it should.

provenance.description: Where a field's value came from, as `InferenceProvenance`: required, not optional, for the same reason the TaskProfile makes it required — an absent trace and a forgotten one are indistinguishable.

origin.description: `InferenceOrigin`'s three values, spelled as that type spells them: `user-stated` means the goal said it, `derived` means a compile concluded it, `default` means nothing decided it. `stated` would let a conclusion present itself as the user's own words.

carries.description: What crosses the channel: the producer's result, a summary of it, or an artifact reference.

retention.description: How long the receiver may keep it: for the step it was read in, for the run, or durably.

taskProfileRef.description: The compiled TaskProfile this node executes under, as its digest (`TaskProfileRef`).

requirementId.description: The requirement inside that profile this node exists to satisfy. acceptance[1] asks that every node be traceable to one, so it is required and not nullable.

kind.description: Why the order holds: the second needs the first's result, or it must merely start after it.

spec.description: `WorldSpecDigest` — the world's own pinned identity, not a copy of its eight dimensions.

dimension.description: One of the eight dimensions `BudgetAmounts` names, in its order.

verificationContractRef.description: must[3]'s versioned extension point. A plan names the contract version it was compiled against; a later contract raises `version` and leaves earlier plans meaning what they meant.

action.description: What to do when that node fails: try it again, run the named alternative, or give up and let `terminal` decide the run's disposition.
